title: validate_patch reported a false 0-nodes on every bare Defs/ xpath
The Scald plume alone saturates rainfall, soaking 325 tiles that are not jungle

text: Measured live 2026-08-21 after the paint. ashkarr_paint.py:481 computes rain_src = clip((0.35 + 3.6*lift) * moist * dayside + 2.6*scald_plume, 0.02, None). The plume term is added UNGATED - it is not multiplied by dayside or moist - and scald_plume peaks at 1.0, so that term alone reaches 2.6. Line 902 then computes rain = 18 + 1650*clip(rain_src/2.6,0,1)**2.2, whose ceiling is exactly 1668. So every tile within about 15 degrees of the Scald point saturates the rainfall scale regardless of its biome, elevation or whether it is lava. 596 tiles sit at the 1668 ceiling, 2.7 percent of the planet. 271 are AB_FeraliskInfestedJungle and that is the DESIGN - the Scald pumps water and makes the one jungle corridor. The other 325 are not: 78 ZBiome_Badlands, 52 ExtremeDesert, 52 ZBiome_DesertOasis, 36 ZBiome_Grasslands, 31 AB_PyroclasticConflagration, 28 Desert, 23 Volcano, 15 LavaField, 6 AB_MiasmicMangrove, 4 AridShrubland. The whole volcanic province, 69 tiles, reads as the wettest ground on the planet. 258 desert-family tiles carry over 600mm against a floor of 18. The paint itself is NOT at fault - seven tiles read back from the engine matched the CSV to the digit.

I never read the response. Twice. THE LAW IS READ THE RETURN VALUE, and I applied it rigorously to every write I made tonight and not once to a call I expected to succeed. The settle-window commit is not wrong in itself - the forty-second window is real and documented - but it was written to explain a symptom that had a different cause, and it would have taught the next reader the wrong lesson. title: 23 of 54 kinds field a bare pawn in 5 rolls; the audit checks the ceiling and cannot see the roll

text: Measured live 2026-08-21: 54 arming kinds spawned 5 times each, 270 pawns, equipment read via jawa/pawn_get. 31 kinds are 5/5. 23 field at least one bare pawn. Worst: Jawa_Empire_Grunt 2/3, Jawa_Blackstar_Grunt 3/5, Jawa_Deepwater_Heavy 3/5, Jawa_Droid_Specialist 3/5, Jawa_Hutt_Leader 3/5, Jawa_Junkers_Grunt 3/5, Jawa_TradeMoot_Grunt 3/5. Spot-verified: the two bare Blackstar grunts are Adults aged 28 and 36 wearing 4 and 6 pieces of apparel with empty hands - fully generated pawns carrying nothing. THE MECHANISM, and it is why the static audit disagrees: jawa/pawnkind_audit uses the engine own eligibility table and reports ZERO broken kinds. It is correct and it answers a different question - can this kind AFFORD its cheapest eligible weapon, which is about the tag pool and the budget CEILING. weaponMoney is a RANGE. A low roll lands below the cheapest weapon the tags allow and the pawn arrives empty-handed, so a kind that is healthy on paper still fields bare hands some fraction of the time. THE FIX IS THE FLOOR, NOT THE CEILING: raise weaponMoney.min to at least the cheapest eligible weapon for each of the 23, which the audit already reports per kind as cheapestPrice. ⛔ Do NOT raise the max - that inflates combatPower by the generator own rule and re-tiers the raids, which is the trap ROLE_KINDS_ARMED_5_OF_5_1 already warns about for the four droid kinds.

spec: Measured 2026-08-21 on DROID_KINDS_NEED_A_RACE_1. `rimflow reassign` only sets `item.owner` (model.py:653); it does not touch `item.state`. Reassigning an item that is `doing` therefore leaves it `doing` under the NEW owner, and `priority.rank()` filters `state != "ready"` (priority.py:82,115) — so the receiving seat is never offered it and has no way to discover it short of `rimflow show` on an ID nobody told them. I worked around it by re-running `claim --seat BUILD`, which routes through the `to("ready" if _complete(item) else "proposed")` branch at model.py:619 — but that fabricates a claim event under a seat that did not act, which is worse than the bug. Pick a real fix: either `reassign` resets a `doing` item to `ready`/`proposed` by the same completeness test `claim` uses, or it refuses outright and names `drop`+`file` as the supported route. ⛔ Do not make `next` surface `doing` items generally — the work stop of 2026-08-21 10:54 depends on parked `doing` items staying unoffered.

The line is [JawaBench] ready: N tools, build <12 hex>, emitted from a MODULE INITIALIZER in JawaBenchInit.cs. 🔑 Not a static constructor, and the difference is the whole point: a static ctor fires on the first tool INVOCATION, by which time somebody has already brought the bridge up and connected - which is the expensive route this item exists to replace. A module initializer runs when the ASSEMBLY IS LOADED, which is the event worth witnessing. ⚠️ net472's reference assemblies have no ModuleInitializerAttribute, so it is declared in JawaBenchInit.cs under System.Runtime.CompilerServices; Roslyn matches it by full name and LangVersion=latest in the csproj is what makes C# 9 module initializers available at all. Do not move that attribute into the JawaBench namespace. THE COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT CONSTANT: it reflects over the assembly for methods carrying RimBridgeServer.Sdk.ToolAttribute, the same rule the bridge itself uses, so it can never drift from the number that gets registered. Source carries 119 [Tool( declarations with --gm; fire_incident and send_letter are compiled out without it, so a non-gm build should report two fewer - which makes the line a check on the BUILD FLAG as well as on loading. ⚠️ ReflectionTypeLoadException is caught separately and the line still prints from the types that DID load, with a warning - a partial load is exactly when a line is most needed. Turning it off would not remove one Gestor from one inspect pane. (2) THE WORD COMES FROM A HARMONY POSTFIX ON Pawn.MainDesc. Pawn_MainDesc_Patch runs for every humanlike pawn, unconditionally, and is not gated by any setting: it takes GenderUtilities.GetGenderPrefix(pawn) - which returns the language keys SEX_HasFemaleOrgan/HasMaleOrgan/HasBothOrgans/HasNoOrgan, i.e. gestor/phallor/aphrodor/neuter - and either replaces the gender word with prefix + gender or prepends it. (3) THE SPECIES WORD WAS NEVER IN THAT LINE. Vanilla Pawn.MainDesc (Verse/Pawn.cs:4303) builds gender, age, kindLabel and optionally faction. It contains no xenotype at all. So "the species word is gone from the pane players read most" is not what happened - nothing was displaced, a word was added in front. The species still reads correctly everywhere it ever read, which the item measured itself. (4) EVERY PAWN GETS A CLASS REGARDLESS OF GENES. GenderUtilities.GetGenderBasedReproductivesForPawn assigns one at generation from gender plus the cross chances; genes only override it, and only 6 of 139 xenotypes in the live dump carry any SEX_ gene. That is why 100% of sampled pawns showed a class - not because integration was on. ⇒ THE REAL LEVERS, in cost order: (a) accept it; (b) OVERRIDE THE FOUR LANGUAGE KEYS in our own mod Languages/English/Keyed - they are plain translatable strings, our mod loads last, no assembly and no setting involved, and the vocabulary becomes ours; (c) a Harmony patch of our own to unpatch Pawn_MainDesc_Patch. ⛔ Do NOT set the keys to empty strings: MatchCasing does char.ToUpper(prefix[0]) with no empty guard, so an empty prefix throws IndexOutOfRange inside a postfix on a label getter - a red error every time a pawn name renders.

DONE 2026-08-22. TEMPERATURE: handled as a hard filter inside the cast - a creature must tolerate its biome's INTERQUARTILE range, not its median. The median alone put cows on sea ice, because SeaIce inherited the -2C LIQUID-water clamp from tiles that had just been frozen. Chasing that revealed SeaIce was two places and split it into SeaIce (frozen shallow sea, -4C) and IceSheet (ancient dark pools, -52C). DIET: six biomes would have starved or eaten themselves. SeaIce had 14 herbivores at plantDensity 0, IceSheet 12; ZBiome_DesertOasis had MORE PREDATORS THAN PREY at 1.07. Two constraints added to the allocator - a barren biome (plantDensity <= 0.02) drops strict vegetarians and keeps omnivores, and carnivores are capped at 40% of a cast. Six problems became one. THE SURVIVOR IS DELIBERATE: IceSheet sits at 0.86 predators-to-prey and that is CORRECT - it has no plants, so its fauna must be carnivores and omnivores, and a real polar ecosystem is marine-fed with the prey off-map. Do not 'fix' it by adding herbivores that would starve. Cost: 754 -> 746 assignments, and AB_FeraliskInfestedJungle is one large and one huge short because the carnivore cap bit on a jungle that was almost all predators. That is the cap working.

MEASURED 2026-08-22, AND THE PREMISE WAS WRONG. This item assumed creatures drawn from four mods balanced against four different games would produce a threat curve nobody designed. Measured across the 621 cast creatures, they do not. THE LADDER IS ALREADY CLEAN: median health-proxy (baseHealthScale x baseBodySize) runs 0.08 / 0.35 / 1.36 / 5.0 / 20.0 / 99.5 across tiny/small/med/large/huge/SUPER - a consistent ~4x step. The size pyramid IS a threat ladder and it did not need building. Donor mods agree closely too: within the 'large' band the median runs 5.0 (Jurassic) to 9.4 (Megafauna) - a 1.9x spread, not the order of magnitude feared. ONLY FOUR creatures of 621 sit 2+ bands from where their body size placed them: thrumborat (bodySize 1.5, healthScale 13, hits like a huge), revenant (healthScale 10), arcturan sky eel (healthScale 3 at bodySize 0.25), bulbfreak (healthScale 0.3 at bodySize 3.5 - a huge creature made of paper). Two of those are Anomaly entities whose stats are deliberately strange and one is a VGE thrumbo hybrid, deliberately tanky in its own mod. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT globally renormalise. Reband or accept those four and leave the other 617 alone. The SUPER outliers - war wyrm 375 and greater krayt dragon 300 against a band median of 99.5 - are SET PIECES, and being an outlier is what a set piece is for. A yardstick still needs writing down if anyone rebalances later, and the ladder above IS that yardstick.

spec: src/RimMandrake/Utils/refresh.py line 744 builds the sqlite path as os.path.join(D_DUMP, 'defs.sqlite') where D_DUMP is game_paths.DEF_DUMP, which resolves to the CAPTURE directory '.../DefDump/captures/2026-08-21T22-44-59Z'. title: Three vanilla biomes are gated on a retexture mod, because the packageId guard credits whoever patched the def last
spec: Found while verifying the BiomeCast fix offline, 2026-08-22 23:5x. NOT firing today - grimterra.terrainretexturemod is active in ModsConfig.xml, so the cast applies. ## The defect - gen_cast_patch.py emits MayRequire=grimterra.terrainretexturemod on Desert, ExtremeDesert and AridShrubland. All three are VANILLA biomes, present in C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Steam\\steamapps\\common\\RimWorld\\Data\\Core\\Defs\\BiomeDefs\\Biomes_WarmArid.xml, and should carry no MayRequire at all - the ludeon.* strip never fired because the packageId lookup did not return ludeon.rimworld. ## Cause - the new packageId guard is PKG.setdefault(defName, packageId) walking captures newest-first, so the OWNER of a def is taken to be whoever the capture last saw defining it. A mod that merely PATCHES a vanilla def appears as its owner. That is wrong for every vanilla def any active mod patches, not only these three. ## Consequence if it stays - disable or unsubscribe the retexture mod and the three desert biomes silently lose their entire animal cast. No error, no log line: MayRequire on a non-present packageId makes the game skip the def quietly. On a desert world that is most of the planet. ## What to check - whether the def dump records a def's DEFINING mod separately from the mods that patch it. If it does not, the fix is a ludeon.* allowlist keyed on the Core/DLC def files rather than on the dump's packageId. ## Watch out - do not just strip every MayRequire; the modded biomes genuinely need theirs, and this same guard was added to stop MayRequire being DROPPED from 26 biomes.

text: PROVEN NARROWED, NOT DISABLED - 2026-08-23 10:2x, and it did NOT need the frozen CSV or a subcount-7 world after all. I said earlier that running world_lint on the wrong world was useless because a clean zero cannot tell a working narrow from a dead check. That was right about a PASSIVE reading and wrong about the item: the answer is to CREATE the population rather than look for one. THE EXPERIMENT, on the throwaway quicktest world: baseline landBiomeSubmerged = 0 across 3,787 tiles scanned, 14 total findings. Then two tiles were written with jawa/world_tile_set and committed - tile 500 set to biome Lake at elevation -50, tile 501 set to biome BorealForest at elevation -50 - both read back confirming the write. RESULT: landBiomeSubmerged went 0 -> 1, total findings 14 -> 15, and the single example row is {tile: 501, biome: BorealForest, elevation: -50.0}. ⇒ THE LAKE BELOW SEA LEVEL WAS NOT FLAGGED AND THE LAND BIOME BELOW SEA LEVEL WAS.
